- If sentiment is high (≥0.7) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce peak predictions to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and forecast is falling, avoid excessive downward bias — price may rebound.  
- When true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% in 3–5 consecutive days, adjust next forecast downward by 1–2% to account for mean reversion.  
- If forecast spikes after a low sentiment period, cap the overshoot at +3% above recent 7-day average to prevent overcorrection.  
- If forecast consistently underestimates true price during high sentiment, add 0.5–1.0% to forecast for the next 3 days to capture sentiment-driven momentum.  
- Avoid forecasting beyond 10% above recent 14-day high — sentiment often corrects quickly after spikes.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows, model should not overfit to recent trend — use 3-day moving average for smoothing.
